item.title: 'Energy ceasefire' agreed between Russia and Ukraine, Trump says
item.description: After Donald Trump's criticism blaming Volodymyr Zelenskyy for high diesel prices, suggesting Ukraine should get a new leader, US President announced Russia and Ukraine had agreed on an 'energy ceasefire'.

item.title: Hochvogel mountain at risk of major collapse as 400,000 cubic metres of rock threatens to break away
item.description: The Hochvogel sits on the border between Germany and the Austrian region of Tyrol. It is part of the Allgäu High Alps and stands at 2,592 metres high.

item.title: 'Up to our people' to pick leader, Zelenskyy responds to Trump's pledge for new elections in Ukraine
item.description: Only Russia is responsible for the war in Ukraine, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday in a TV interview, responding to criticism from US President Donald Trump, who blamed him for high diesel prices and said he should be replaced.

item.title: At least 139 migrants dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
item.description: The UN's IOM agency says tens of thousands of migrants travel from the Horn of Africa through Djibouti each year as they look to cross the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Yemen and eventually reach the Gulf countries.

item.title: Russian army strikes Sloviansk and Kyiv as Ukrainian drones hit third Yandex data centre
item.description: Russian forces struck two apartment blocks in Sloviansk, injuring four, and hit warehouses in Kyiv. Overnight, Ukrainian drones targeted Yandex's data centre in Vladimir, causing major service outages but no casualties.

item.title: Riyadh airport stays shut after deadly attack as Trump says US may join Saudi strikes on Houthis
item.description: An attack that killed 12 people has left Riyadh’s airport closed and drawn condemnation from the UN and EU, as the Houthis renew their threats and Washington considers its response.

item.title: Macron's popularity hits lowest level since 2017 as Bardella and Le Pen also lose ground
item.description: Some 82% of French people now disapprove of the president. Meanwhile, Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella are weakened by Mediapart's revelations about antisemitic texts attributed to the young RN leader.

item.title: Denmark tests humanoid robots in supermarkets to help to ease staff workload at night
item.description: Denmark’s Salling Group is trialling Hive Robots in stores to handle demanding restocking, freeing staff for customer service while robots work mainly at night.

item.title: Zaporizhzhia airstrikes kill 17 as Russia intensifies attacks across Ukraine
item.description: Zaporizhzhia was hit by deadly Russian airstrikes on Saturday, 10 October, killing at least 17 people, including three children, Ukrainian officials said. Rescuers searched rubble for survivors as the city faced renewed strikes on residential areas.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV to have surgery in 'coming days' to remove nodule in lung
item.description: "It was detected at a very early stage and is well localised," the pontiff said during an address in St. Peter's Square.

item.title: US police criticise Anthropic after Claude AI submits false information about an unsolved murder
item.description: The US police called the delay in detecting and reporting the incident “unacceptable”, but said there was no indication of unauthorised access to their systems or compromised data.

item.title: Polish police alerted over possible attack on PM Donald Tusk
item.description: It remains unclear what information the police received or what form the potential threat may have taken.

item.title: Czech PM Babiš's ANO faces strong challenge in first round of Senate election
item.description: “Five senators were elected in the first round, equalling the historic record set in 2024,” Eva Krumpová, first deputy chair of the Czech Statistics Office, said. Of the five candidates to win seats outright, none were from the ANO.

item.title: Protesters take to the streets in Portugal over rising living costs and housing prices
item.description: A post from an Instagram account appearing to be linked to the protests that had promoted the demonstrations said people had "been squeezed by rising house prices and the cost of living" for years.

item.title: Four dead as Isaias continues to push across the Southeast US, bringing strong winds and heavy rain
item.description: Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 hurricane in the city of Destin in the Florida Panhandle on Friday evening. It has since weakened into a post-tropical cyclone.

item.title: Teen revolt or revolution? The student protests threatening France's presidential race
item.description: French students' grievances include long school days, overcrowded classrooms, outdated facilities and teacher shortages. Their anger has resonated across Europe, with students in Belgium and Italy also staging protests.

item.title: Farming and solar power are competing for land. Can agrivoltaics solve the problem?
item.description: Agrivoltaics could help to prevent farmland abandonment by protecting crops and boosting income. But some say the solution ignores the real problems.

item.title: Europe's best Christmas markets to visit in 2026, according to travellers
item.description: Europe is world-famous for its Christmas markets, and more than 1,500 take place every year. Choosing which to visit can be as tricky as putting together your present wish list. Here are the top picks, as voted for by travellers.

item.title: ESA director general reveals €10bn plan to get to space without NASA
item.description: The space industry, currently valued at €600 billion, is expected to grow by 10% a year, according to European Space Agency (ESA) director general Josef Aschbacher. He spoke to the Big Question about how Europe can benefit from this booming industry.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 11th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Trump says Ukraine needs new president after Zelenskyy condemns Russia fuel deal
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Ukraine needs a new president and blamed Ukraine's leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy for high US diesel prices.

item.title: Lee Claims World Gold as Tasoev Secures His Third World Title in Baku
item.description: Hyeonji Lee claimed her first world title at +78kg, defeating former champion Romane Dicko to complete a dominant day. At +100kg, Inal Tasoev delivered a spectacular ippon against home favourite Ushangi Kokauri to secure his third world title and retain the red backpatch.

item.title: Spanish PM Sánchez launches campaign with housing as key theme
item.description: Pedro Sánchez kicked off his 29 November campaign in the so-called "lucky city" of Dos Hermanas in Seville before some 5,000 people.

item.title: Left-wing primary: more than half of registered voters have already voted, say organisers
item.description: Some 140,000 voters are choosing between five rivals for the Socialist nomination, hoping to influence France's 2027 presidential election; after a cyberattack, voting now runs until Sunday 6pm.

item.title: Pope Leo condemns death penalty, Vance vows not to watch Hasan’s execution live
item.description: Without explicitly referring to the scheduled execution of the Fort Hood killer, the Pope reiterates the Church’s opposition to the death penalty. In the US, Vice-President Vance says he will not watch the execution by firing squad, which is due to be live-streamed in December

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo suspended by Portuguese FA for leaving training camp
item.description: As expected, the Disciplinary Board of the Portuguese Football Federation has opened disciplinary proceedings against national team captain Cristiano Ronaldo, who has been temporarily suspended.

item.title: 12 killed and more than 300 wounded in attack on Riyadh airport
item.description: Turki Al-Maliki, a spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition forces, said that the attack had been carried out by Yemen's Houthi rebels and that it had targeted a passenger terminal.

item.title: Thousands detained in New Delhi as police crack down on 'cockroach' movement
item.description: Police detained “cockroach movement” leader Abhijeet Dipke and two others as hundreds of protesters defied a heavy security clampdown in New Delhi.

item.title: Palestinian President Abbas postpones legislative elections until September 2027
item.description: On Friday, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar accused Abbas of "fooling the international community by canceling once again promised elections" as rumours of the postponement circulated.

item.title: Czechs head to polls in local and Senate elections
item.description: Andrej Babiš, the country's billionaire populist PM and founder of the Agrofert food and chemicals group, will be hoping his party can make gains in the 81-seat Senate.

item.title: EU budget: Ireland pitches €141bn cuts to appease the ‘frugals’
item.description: Ireland proposes cutting the next EU budget by 8%, with global cooperation and competitiveness taking the deepest cuts, while agriculture and cohesion funding is reduced by only 3%. It also includes a €55bn-a-year package of own resources. EU leaders will discuss the plan on 15-16 October.

item.title: Panic in Panama as 7.7 quake hits, cathedral collapses and tsunami warnings spread
item.description: Panama was hit by a powerful 7.7 earthquake, a 6.6 aftershock and many tremors, damaging buildings and prompting evacuations but no deaths reported.

item.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill at least 20, including three children
item.description: Ukrainian national police said Russian forces had targeted residential areas of Zaporizhzhia with five guided aerial bombs early on Saturday, with two of them striking blocks of flats.

item.title: 'No one ever heard of her': Trump goes off on petty rant after Nobel Peace Prize snub
item.description: Trump claimed he "should have won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes" for having "settled 8 wars" as he dismissed Pillay's career in an irate Truth Social post.

item.title: Silent killer: study finds most with high blood pressure unaware
item.description: Men showed higher rates of hypertension, with 42% affected compared with 29% of women, after adjusting the figures for age groups.

item.title: Life-threatening Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida, bringing high winds and heavy rain
item.description: The US' National Weather Service (NWS) has warned a life-threatening storm surge is expected from Dauphin Island, Alabama, to Suwannee, Florida.

item.title: As Russia escalates its war, the EU realises its support for Ukraine won't be enough
item.description: Russia's rapid escalation has thrown into doubt the European Union's multiple support programmes for Ukraine. Diplomats concede it is only a matter of time before leaders address the contentious matter.

item.title: 'Crashout', 'Ragebait' or 'Peak': Want to know which word is favoured by Germany's youth?
item.description: The three frontrunners 'Crashout', 'Ragebait' and 'Peak' are in the running to become Germany's youth word of the year 2026, with anglicisms particularly trendy. The winning term will be announced this Saturday at the Frankfurt Book Fair.

item.title: When will El Niño peak and end? A full timeline of the weather phenomenon taking the world by storm
item.description: A ‘Godzilla’ El Niño is still intensifying in the Pacific. When will we see the weather phenomenon peak – and when will it come to an end?

item.title: Which Europeans post the most holiday selfies? Study reveals travellers’ social media habits
item.description: Research by Opodo has revealed how social media is impacting the way we travel. From choosing what to post to not being engaged at all, here are the trends identified by the study.

item.title: Teacher salaries in Europe: Which countries offer the best pay?
item.description: Teacher salaries vary widely across Europe, and large gaps remain even after adjusting for living costs. Experts call for better pay to attract and retain more teachers.

item.title: Police clash with protesters in Brussels as thousands march against spending cuts
item.description: Clashes broke out between police and protesters in Brussels on Friday, 9 October, as thousands marched against the Belgian government's planned spending cuts. Police estimated that 30,000 people took part in the demonstration, organised by trade unions amid growing opposition to austerity measures.

item.title: Zelenskyy hits out at 'gifts to Putin' after Trump announces deal for Russian diesel
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Russian leader Vladimir Putin had agreed to release diesel into US and global markets.

item.title: Historic Gold for Lytvynenko as Sulamanidze Triumphs in Baku
item.description: Yelyzaveta Lytvynenko made history at -78kg, defeating Kaila Issoufi to become the UAE’s first-ever judo world champion. At -100kg, Georgia’s Ilia Sulamanidze overcame Dota Arai in the final to claim his first world title, turning previous bronze into gold.

item.title: Powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama, damaging buildings and injuring at least 27
item.description: Local footage showed a cathedral collapsing and a hotel facade falling onto a car in Penonomé, central Panama.

item.title: Flydubai co-pilot planned suicide attack in Tel Aviv airport inspired by 9/11
item.description: The Omani co-pilot was previously barred from flying in Oman over extremist views.
